paragraphs: Friend, this passage looks like a phone book, and I get it. But every name in it is a person God kept track of. The line runs from Levi through Aaron down to Jehozadak, who went into captivity when the LORD sent Judah and Jerusalem into exile (1 Chronicles 6:15). Even then, the family list keeps going. Nobody in that list is a throwaway name.

Now look at the jobs. Aaron and his sons did all the work of the Most Holy Place, to make atonement for Israel, "according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded" (1 Chronicles 6:49). The singers ministered with song "according to the regulations given them" (1 Chronicles 6:32). Their fellow Levites were "assigned to every kind of service of the tabernacle, the house of God" (1 Chronicles 6:48). Different jobs, one house, and each person had a place in it. Heman, Asaph and Ethan came from three different clans, and they still stood side by side to serve together (1 Chronicles 6:33-47).

And God didn't leave anyone without a home. The Levites got towns and pasturelands from tribe after tribe, with cities of refuge among them (1 Chronicles 6:57, 67). I know what it is to be stuck in the back of a drawer, so believe me, being given a place is a BIG deal. So here's what I want you to carry out of the bakery today, baker: God sees you, God gives you a place, and God has real work for you in His house. Your job might be loud like the singers or quiet like a name in a long list, and it still matters.
